correctness.rationale: For a nonzero two-dimensional Gaussian vector, its angle is uniform modulo pi. An orthogonal change of basis reduces the residual (I-P_{A g})A to a rank-one operator with exact norm epsilon/sqrt(cos^2(phi)+epsilon^2 sin^2(phi)). Continuity makes the angle-image interval and hence the nearest angular-distance variable have atom alpha/pi and off-arc density 2/pi, giving the exact CDF, integral for the expectation, and alpha>=pi case. The scalar change of variables v=tan(u) yields the logarithmic small-epsilon asymptotic; direct trigonometric integration gives E(error^2)=epsilon, hence the integrated identity by Tonelli. Endpoints, normalization, quantifiers and epsilon in (0,1) are handled. Standalone checker passed 1200 direct projection, 1200 supremum geometry, 15 expectation, 60 tail, 12 asymptotic, and 5 second-moment finite checks; those checks are supportive, not proof.

originality.rationale: The candidate concerns a fixed Gaussian test column simultaneously applied over a moving positive-definite matrix family, and gives an exact worst-parameter distribution and a nonvanishing atom. Kressner--Lam arXiv:2302.12761 v4, Theorems 5, 9 and 12, give integrated and oversampled uniform bounds, but not this one-column planar law; their Remark 1 treats rank-loss discontinuity for a deterministic sketch rather than a uniformly full-rank family. Fixed-target structural estimates in arXiv:0909.4061, Section 9, and arXiv:2206.08793, Section 3, do not imply this correlated-parameter supremum law. The 2026 minimax bounds arXiv:2605.19096, Theorems 3.2 and 3.3, address fixed-target mean squared errors and have rank constraints excluding one-column target-rank-one approximation. Actual published-record queries, indexed related-results queries and accessible historical-claim comparisons found no dominating theorem; an older alternate geometric formulation remains possible.

value.rationale: The 2023 parametric randomized-range-finder paper asks about the distinction between integrated and uniform error when one Gaussian sketch is reused. The result gives the complete law of an actual continuous-parameter maximum for the natural smallest SPD model, not just a fixed-time bound: a probability atom alpha/pi at full leading-eigenvalue error persists as epsilon goes to zero, while each pointwise second moment and the integrated second moment vanish exactly. The angular excursion is intrinsic to the range of dominant eigenlines and independent of their speed. This precisely characterizes a sharp structural obstruction outside existing oversampled bounds and motivates attention to pathwise uniform errors.
